title: Iterative model benchmarking and traffic-phasing framework
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and deliver a reusable framework for running iterative A/B and canary experiments across model versions that focuses on phased traffic ramping, cohort-aware metrics, and automated rollback triggers. The goal is to give product teams a low-friction way to validate model quality and cost trade-offs in production while minimizing user impact and operational toil.
background: Current model rollout patterns at Redwood are fragmented: ad-hoc canaries, manual traffic splits, and separate monitoring dashboards. This causes slow rollouts, inconsistent statistical checks, and delayed rollback decisions. Existing PM work (see PM-5120 family) focuses on exposure controllers; this ticket unifies runbooks, statistical decision rules, and an infra-facing API for phased traffic. We also need to support heterogeneous cohorts (different latency and interaction patterns) and shadow verification for riskier variants.
proposal: Ship a 3-part framework: (1) Experiment composer (API + UI) to define cohorts, metrics, priors, and phasing policy; (2) Traffic phaser: enforcement engine that performs stepwise traffic increases with TTLs, decay/backoff, and cohort-weight adjustments; (3) Safety evaluator: an online statistical module that runs sequential checks (Bayesian sequential testing + drift detector) and emits actions (continue, pause, rollback) with confidence scores. Integrate with Console for visualization and with Dedicated/Private routing for enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Teams can create an experiment via API or Console specifying cohorts, metrics, and a 4-step phasing policy
Traffic phaser can enforce percent traffic splits per cohort and automatically apply next phase after passing statistical checks
Safety evaluator runs sequential tests and outputs machine-readable actions (ALLOW, PAUSE, ROLLBACK) with a human-readable rationale
Shadow verification pipeline can mirror 100% of traffic to a variant without affecting responses and emit discrepancy metrics
End-to-end playbook documented in Confluence with run examples and GitHub PRs linked
SLO for evaluation latency < 5s (decision emitted) for 95th percentile under production load

metrics: Time-to-decision (median and p95) for a canary phase
User-facing error rate delta for cohort vs control
Cost per 1M tokens for variant vs baseline
Experiment throughput: concurrent experiments supported per region
statistical_checks: Primary: Bayesian sequential A/B test on user-impact metric with adaptive alpha (default alpha=0.05, min samples per cohort 500)
Secondary: non-parametric rank test for latency distributions (handles heavy tails)
Drift detector: EWT-based distribution shift detector on prompt embeddings and token-level distributions
Cohort-weighted aggregation: account for heterogeneous cohorts with inverse-variance weighting
Early-stop rules: stop when posterior probability that variant is worse > 98% for primary metric
Safety bands: set absolute thresholds (error rate + latency) that trigger immediate rollback regardless of statistical state
rollout_plan: Stage 0 — Shadow: mirror 100% of traffic for 48h, no user exposure; run discrepancy and regression checks
Stage 1 — Canary 1%: route 1% traffic for 6h, run sequential checks; require pass on primary metric and no safety band breaches
Stage 2 — Canary 5%: route 5% traffic for 12h; require pass and stable cost delta < 20%
Stage 3 — Canary 20%: route 20% traffic for 24h; run full metric suite including business KPIs
Stage 4 — Ramp to 100%: incremental steps to 50% then 100% with watch windows and manual approval guardrail
Rollback: immediate rollback to last stable model if safety band triggered or if safety evaluator issues ROLLBACK action
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy metrics from small cohorts — Mitigation: require min sample sizes and cohort-weighted tests
Risk: excessive cost during shadow runs — Mitigation: sampling policy configurable per experiment
Risk: incorrect decisions due to distributional shift — Mitigation: add drift detector and use recent priors
Risk: operator confusion — Mitigation: clear Console rationale, explanation of tests, and automated runbook suggestions
